title: First car, first visit
role: New grad, parents helping with the down payment
recommend: 2026 RVR ES AWC, or Eclipse Cross ES if she wants the turbo
hidden: Her parents told her to buy a Corolla because "it holds its value".

beats.say: Hi. I'm just looking. I've never bought a car before.

choices.text: Welcome in, Priya. What do you need the car to do, and who else is part of this?
choices.reply: My parents are helping with the down payment. They have opinions.

choices.text: The RVR is on special. Want to start there?
choices.reply: Maybe. I don't really know what the differences are.

choices.text: You look like an Eclipse Cross person. Come sit down.
choices.reply: I... okay. I guess.

beats.say: I drive to work in Vancouver most days. Just me. Sometimes my sister.

choices.text: How many kilometres on a normal day, and do you park outside at home?
choices.reply: About forty. Outside, at my parents' place in Port Coquitlam.

choices.text: Then you want all-wheel drive and a sunroof. Let me show you a loaded one.
choices.reply: That sounds expensive. I had a number in my head.

choices.text: A five-seat SUV can do that. We will check the payment against the help your parents are giving.
choices.reply: They said around eight thousand down. I don't want the payment to scare them.

beats.say: They told me to just get a Corolla. They said it holds its value and Mitsubishi doesn't.

choices.text: They might be right about resale. I won't promise a number three years out. Let's put warranty, winter driving and today's payment beside a Corolla quote.
choices.reply: Okay. That's fairer than I expected.

choices.text: Resale is a myth. Ignore them.
choices.reply: They're paying. I'm not going to ignore them.

choices.text: Our 10-year powertrain is longer than Toyota's 5-year coverage. Want to see the line in the booklet?
choices.reply: If I can show them that on paper, maybe.

beats.say: If I brought them, what would we even sit in? I don't want to waste their Saturday.

choices.text: One car. RVR ES AWC: heated seats, a price that respects the budget, and AWC you can show them in the rain. Eclipse Cross only if you want the turbo more than the lower payment.
choices.reply: The RVR sounds like the one I can defend.

choices.text: We'll look at all six trims so they feel thorough.
choices.reply: They will hate that. My dad gets impatient.

choices.text: Sit in the Outlander GT. Parents like leather.
choices.reply: That payment would end the conversation.

beats.say: So... what happens now?

choices.text: If the RVR ES AWC on the lot fits the payment with their down payment, we write it up subject to them seeing it tonight. What time do they get home?
choices.reply: They're home at six. I can bring them.

choices.text: Take a brochure and think about the whole lineup.
choices.reply: Yeah. I'll... think about it.

choices.text: I can hold the car if you leave a deposit your parents don't know about.
choices.reply: No. I'm not doing that to them.

choices.text: Good. Tell me the number you need this deal to hit, and we'll appraise it properly instead of guessing in the aisle.

choices.text: Trades are a hassle. You'll get more privately.
choices.reply: So you don't want my business.

choices.text: We always beat Toyota by a thousand. Done.
choices.reply: You haven't even looked at it.

beats.say: It has every service record. I don't want someone kicking the tires and shrugging.

choices.text: Records help. We'll do a real walkaround: tires, panels, the service book. I won't insult a car you maintained.
choices.reply: Alright. It's the grey one by the door.

choices.text: Condition barely matters. It's all auction anyway.
choices.reply: Then why would I bother washing it?

choices.text: I'll have the manager glance at it later.
choices.reply: Later usually means a worse number.

beats.say: Be straight. Are you going to lowball me to make the Outlander look cheap?

choices.text: The trade is one number and the Outlander is another. We won't bury a weak appraisal inside a discount. You'll see both.
choices.reply: That's the first straight sentence today.

choices.text: Everyone feels lowballed. Get used to it.
choices.reply: I'm done.

choices.text: If the number is light we can add it back as a discount so the payment looks the same.
choices.reply: That's the same trick.

beats.say: Fine. Why an Outlander instead of another RAV4?

choices.text: Seven seats when the grandkids are here, S-AWC standard, and a 10-year powertrain. Their hybrid will win on fuel. I won't pretend otherwise.
choices.reply: The grandkids are the reason I'm even here.

choices.text: Because Toyota is overpriced and boring.
choices.reply: I've liked that RAV4 for six years. Watch it.

choices.text: The Outlander is nicer. You'll see.
choices.reply: Show me, then.

beats.say: If the appraisal is close to that other offer, I'll listen.

choices.text: Let's appraise it now and pick SE or LE based on the camera and the cruise, not on a fantasy number. If we can't land, I'll tell you.
choices.reply: Do the appraisal. I'll wait.

choices.text: Sign the worksheet and we'll adjust the trade after.
choices.reply: No chance.

choices.text: Come back tomorrow and ask for the used-car manager.
choices.reply: I have time now. Tomorrow I won't.

choices.reply: I don't believe you.

choices.reply: Let's drive it.

choices.text: The test drive is gas only. EV mode confuses people.
choices.reply: That's the part I came to feel.

choices.text: Sign first, drive at delivery.
choices.reply: No.

choices.text: Six-twenty all-in, or before taxes and extras? And do both kids ride at the same time every day?

choices.text: Payments are easy. We'll stretch the term.
choices.reply: I don't want to still be paying when they're in high school.

choices.text: Let me show you the GT. You can always come down.
choices.reply: I just told you the number.

beats.say: My mother comes on Sundays. The kids are in seats all week. I also have a stroller and a dog.

choices.text: That is an Outlander, not an Eclipse Cross. Third row for your mother on Sunday, folded the rest of the week so the stroller fits. Cargo behind the third row is only about 308 litres.
choices.reply: Good. The last salesperson pretended the back was huge.

choices.text: Seven seats means lots of cargo too. You'll be fine with everything in it.
choices.reply: That can't be true.

choices.text: A five-seat with a roof box is the same thing.
choices.reply: I don't want a roof box in the parkade.

choices.text: Then those go in the first pencil. Taxes, freight, PDI, and winter tires as a line you can say yes or no to. I won't land a payment that can't survive the office.
choices.reply: Please. I'm tired of the second number.

choices.text: Ignore the first quotes. Ours will be different, trust me.
choices.reply: That's what they all say.

choices.text: We can roll the tires in and not show them.
choices.reply: I want to see them.

beats.say: SE or LE? The LE payment might break us.

choices.text: SE has the heated wheel, the liftgate and the sunroof. LE adds the 360 camera and adaptive cruise. If the camera saves a bumper in your parkade, we price it. If not, SE is the honest fit.
choices.reply: The parkade is tight. Price the LE. I'll decide with the real number.

choices.text: Always buy the higher trim. You'll regret SE.
choices.reply: You don't know my budget better than I do.

choices.text: They're basically identical.
choices.reply: Then why is the price different?

beats.say: If the all-in number is under six-fifty I can probably move. Six-twenty was the dream.

choices.text: I'll have the desk build SE and LE, all-in, same down payment, tires shown. You pick with both numbers in front of you. No surprise in the office.
choices.reply: Build them. We'll sit down.

choices.text: Let's do 96 months so six-twenty works, and we'll talk total later.
choices.reply: That's how my brother got stuck.

choices.text: I'll text you a payment tonight.
choices.reply: Text me both, but I'd rather see them now.

choices.text: CR-Vs are dangerous in the mountains.
choices.reply: I've done three seasons in it. Come on.

choices.text: S-AWC is unbeatable. Nothing else gets up that road.
choices.reply: That's an ad.

choices.text: Our AWD is full-time lock, all four wheels, always.

choices.text: Our fuel economy is better than a hybrid. Their site is wrong.
choices.reply: I'm looking at the number right now.

choices.text: Fuel doesn't matter if the car is fun.

beats.say: Warranty. Theirs is fine, isn't it?

choices.reply: Put it on the sheet. They'll ask.

choices.text: We have a lifetime warranty.
choices.reply: No you don't.

choices.text: Warranties are all the same.
choices.reply: Then I might as well stay.

beats.say: It's dry today. How do I even feel the difference?

choices.text: The brochure has a snow photo. That's enough.
choices.reply: I came to drive.

choices.text: You have to buy it to really know.
choices.reply: Absolutely not.

choices.text: We'll add them and you can cancel. It's easier.
choices.reply: No.

beats.say: My rate is 5.9. Be honest if you can't touch it.

choices.text: I don't know today's reserve or special rate. The desk will. If 5.9 wins, we use your credit union and move on.
choices.reply: Alright. Ask them.

choices.text: We can always beat a bank. It's what we do.
choices.reply: There it is.

choices.text: 5.9 is terrible. You should be embarrassed.
choices.reply: We're done talking about my finances.

beats.say: If the GT is in stock and the numbers come back clean, I'll take it this week.

choices.text: Let's confirm the stock unit, the colour, and a delivery time that doesn't depend on a product you don't want. Then the desk brings one page: price, rate comparison, rebate status.
choices.reply: One page. I'll read it.

choices.text: Give me your credit application anyway, just in case.
choices.reply: You said you wouldn't do that.

choices.text: Come back Saturday and start over with another rep.
choices.reply: I'm here now.
